solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Odd non-English words are OK — they slow you down

indicators.note: odd here means strange or irregular, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: non-English says the letter E, short for English, is dropped from the word beside it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that strange foreign words are acceptable because they make a reader go slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-English' takes E out of ARE, leaving AR; 'Odd' then rearranges WORDS + AR + OK.
explanation.definitionFit: Repairs to a road narrow the lanes and force traffic to crawl, so they slow drivers down.

clue.text: Modern car manufacture, British in origin

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for British is placed inside the word for origin

parts.note: a root is an origin or source

explanation.surface: A claim that today's car-making began in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Automated machines on assembly lines do most of the work in building cars today, so they stand for modern car production.

clue.text: Sort of hat a loyal religious leader appears in

indicators.note: to sort is to arrange, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A particular style of headgear in which a faithful cleric is seen.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a senior Shiite Muslim cleric in Iran, a high religious authority.

clue.text: Merchant seaman's predicament takes priority, we're told

indicators.note: we're told signals that the letters are a spoken version of the words, matched by ear

parts.note: a predicament is a hole and a seaman a sailor; the predicament taking priority puts HOLE first, giving HOLE SAILOR

explanation.surface: A merchant sailor's plight comes first, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: HOLE SAILOR, said quickly, gives the trader's title.
explanation.definitionFit: A merchant who buys goods in bulk and sells them on to shops is a wholesale trader.

clue.text: Possibly spreads out in the west

definitions.text: Possibly spreads out in the west

parts.words: Possibly spreads out in the west
parts.note: in American usage a spread is a large farm, and the big cattle farms of the US West are typical examples

explanation.surface: Something that perhaps sprawls over the land in the western states.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreads' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: US slang for big farms.
explanation.definitionFit: A spread is American slang for a large farm or estate, so cattle farms in the West are examples.

clue.text: Soil surrounds us and gives support

indicators.note: surrounds says the soiling word goes around the letters of us

parts.note: to soil something is to stain it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Earth wraps around us and holds us up.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolster or hold something up is to give it support, as in to keep someone going.

clue.text: Leader abandons modest expedition

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, and it abandons the word, so the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: chaste means pure or modest

explanation.surface: A chief walks out on a humble journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expedition' here means speed, not a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedition in its older sense means promptness or speed in doing something, a synonym of hurry.

clue.text: Go uphill — it's a must for climbers

definitions.meaning: to make for higher ground is to aim one's course upwards
climbers need to be free of vertigo, comfortable at altitude

explanation.surface: Climb the hill, because a strong stomach for altitude is essential for mountaineers.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb phrase it means set off towards high places; as a noun phrase it means freedom from fear of altitude.

clue.text: Girl entertains, say, with this musical link

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them, so the girl's name holds the other piece

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name
say means for example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: A woman hosts guests and uses this to join two pieces of music.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a smooth transition from one piece into the next without a pause is called by this name.

clue.text: Precision perfomance welcomed by one-time head

indicators.note: welcomed by says the performance word is taken in by the words that follow

parts.note: ex means former or one-time
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness
an act is a performance (the clue misspells the word)

explanation.surface: A precise show is received warmly by a former chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is a headland (NESS), not a boss. The clue's 'perfomance' is a typo for performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactness and precision are synonyms, both meaning accuracy in every detail.

clue.text: Party's instruction to vote against?

definitions.meaning: British slang for a lively party or celebration
read as ..., it tells someone to cast a vote against

explanation.surface: A political party's whip telling members to oppose a motion.
explanation.definitionFit: Beano is British informal for a party or spree, and split up it orders a no vote.

clue.text: Drunk lost again in reminiscence

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters stagger about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy gets lost once more while reminiscing.
explanation.definitionFit: A wistful longing for the past is the feeling behind reminiscing, so the two are close synonyms.

clue.text: Where wine and spirits may go … and success also

definitions.text: Where wine and spirits may go … and success also

parts.words: Where wine and spirits may go … and success also
parts.note: drink can make one dizzy, and triumph can make one conceited, both expressed with the same idiom

explanation.surface: Alcohol goes somewhere, and so can triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says something intoxicates, literally from drink or figuratively from success making a person vain.

clue.text: Expert with poor marks on paper

parts.note: D and E are low grades in an exam
FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: A specialist given low grades on an essay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paper' is a newspaper, the FT, the very one printing this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Deft means skilful or adroit, as an expert is.

clue.text: See 6
A primarily lonely old king's listening closely

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of lonely is used

parts.note: Lear is the legendary old king of Shakespeare's play, plus the 's

explanation.surface: A solitary elderly monarch pays close attention.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means paying full attention, as though nothing but ears.

clue.text: Easy money made by one firm throw

parts.note: a means one
fast means firmly fixed, as in hold fast
a horse that bucks throws its rider

explanation.surface: Cash earned by one company with a hard pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom names money made quickly with little effort, the same as easy money; buck is US slang for a dollar.

clue.text: Newborn given gas at end of procedure

parts.note: neon is a noble gas

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of procedure

explanation.surface: A baby is given anaesthetic gas when a medical procedure ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Neonate is the medical term for a newborn infant, in its first weeks of life.

clue.text: Pride shown by Josh's leader in mixed race

indicators.note: in says the leader of Josh goes inside the mixed letters
mixed means the letters of race are stirred into a new order

parts.note: in the curry rogan josh, the word rogan comes before josh

explanation.surface: Someone called Josh, heading a team in a race of mixed ability, shows conceit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Josh' looks like a person, but it comes from rogan josh, an Indian lamb curry, whose first word leads it. 'mixed' shuffles the race letters into ARCE, split open by 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pride in the sense of haughty self-importance is the same as an overbearing manner.

clue.text: To some extent with a coach I eventually succeed

indicators.note: to some extent means partly, so only part of these words gives the letters

explanation.surface: With a trainer, I will in the end do well, at least partly.
explanation.definitionFit: To achieve is to succeed in reaching a goal; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Jewellery item going amiss needs one installing

indicators.note: installing means fitting something in, so the one-letter piece goes inside

parts.note: erring means going wrong or astray
a means one

explanation.surface: A missing piece of jewellery needs a fitter to put one in.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring or stud worn on the lobe is a common item of jewellery.

clue.text: He breaks hearts and is consistent

indicators.note: breaks into means splitting the hearts word to let the other piece in

parts.note: the core of something is its heart
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man who is a heartbreaker, yet steady and reliable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that hangs together logically is consistent, matching the verb to stick together.

clue.text: Change name in secret

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for name inside the secret word

parts.note: covert means secret or hidden

explanation.surface: Swap a name in private.
explanation.definitionFit: To convert something is to change it into another form or use.

clue.text: Break in length of clematis needs cutting back

indicators.note: back says the cut stretch is read in reverse, as one cuts a plant back
a length of something is a piece cut from it, so only a stretch of the word is used

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: the clematis has a gap and needs pruning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break in' is the definition, as in training a horse. EMAT sits inside 'clematis'; 'cutting back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To break in a horse is to tame it, training it to accept a rider.

clue.text: Process aimed to create such studies at university?

indicators.note: to process material is to work it into another form, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A course designed to turn out students of a particular subject.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the clue: such studies are the degree subject named by the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Media studies is a university subject, so the answer is the kind of studies the clue means.

clue.text: The time for last swallows, departing

definitions.text: The time for last swallows, departing

parts.words: The time for last swallows, departing
parts.note: in a British pub, after last orders drinkers get a short period to finish their glasses before leaving

explanation.surface: The season when the final birds fly off south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallows' are the birds of autumn migration on the surface, but here they are gulps of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: British licensing law allows a short period after closing for patrons to finish drinks before going.

clue.text: Dress up like a proper prince

parts.note: prim means prim and proper, stiffly correct

explanation.surface: Put on fine clothes as a well-mannered royal would.
explanation.definitionFit: To preen or smarten oneself fussily is to dress oneself up.

clue.text: Scottish bank starts off brisk recovery after expansion

indicators.note: starts off means the beginnings of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: A Scottish lender begins a quick bounce back after growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' is a slope, not a lender.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots a brae is a hillside or steep slope, as by a river.

clue.text: Foreign articles associated with work cause stress

parts.note: un is a French article and der a German one
a line is a line of work, an occupation

explanation.surface: Imported terms connected with the job lead to anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: To underline a point is to emphasise or stress it.

clue.text: Stern one is heard in India

parts.note: hind means at the back or rear, as a stern is
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A severe person is listened to in India.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the main language of northern India, so it is what one hears spoken there.

clue.text: The villain of the pack

parts.note: the jack in a deck of cards has an old name that also means a rogue

explanation.definitionFit: This word means both a scoundrel and the jack card in a deck.

clue.text: Tired of hearing Nessun dorma? An appropriate response!

definitions.text: Tired of hearing Nessun dorma? An appropriate response!

parts.words: Tired of hearing Nessun dorma? An appropriate response!
parts.note: the aria title Nessun dorma means none shall sleep, so a weary listener does the opposite

explanation.surface: A jaded opera-goer, bored of the famous Puccini aria, nods off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tired' looks like weary of; it is literally sleepy. Nessun dorma, from Puccini's Turandot, means 'none shall sleep'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dozing off is the fitting reply both for the tired and for a song commanding wakefulness.
